requirements.text: TIER 1 - PROGRAM-WIDE POINTERS FILE, AUTO-INJECTED: .claude/rules/PROGRAM_KNOWLEDGE.md exists as an unconditioned rule (no paths: frontmatter) so it auto-injects into EVERY session in this repository at start - orchestrator, companion, and any future session lineage alike. Content = compressed pointers only (names, paths, one-line facts an engineer keeps in their head): hard-won mechanics, key file locations, proven arcs, domain anchors. It GROWS continuously: any session that discovers something program-wide-useful appends it when discovered (never batched to session end). HARD CONSTRAINT: the eager context budget (tools/context_budget_check.py, 6000-token eager total) is the mechanical growth limit - when near it, COMPRESS or demote to Tier 2/docs, never raise the budget as a side effect.
requirements.required_harness: file exists as an unconditioned rule; context_budget_check PASS after every edit to it

requirements.text: TIER 2 - CURRENT-SECTION WORKING KNOWLEDGE FILE, HANDOFF-READ: docs/WORKING_KNOWLEDGE.md exists as a living file scoped to the section of the program currently being built (not injected eagerly; the session handoff and successor prompt name it as a MUST-READ). It carries the localized research, pointers, and state that would otherwise be re-derived: current-lane specifics, in-flight build inputs, section-scoped gotchas. It is CONTINUOUSLY UPDATED during work on the section.
requirements.required_harness: file exists; SESSION_HANDOFF must-read list and successor prompt name it

requirements.text: PRUNE-OR-PROMOTE AT SECTION CLOSE (context stays controlled): when a section finishes, its Tier-2 entries are either DELETED (full text stays in git history) or PROMOTED to Tier 1 in compressed-pointer form if they proved program-wide durable. The active Tier-2 file never carries finished-section material. This is the accepted refinement of the owner's 'you can remove it' instruction (advice invited and given: promote-before-prune so durable knowledge is never lost with the section).
requirements.required_harness: section-close seams (wave close / handoff) show prune-or-promote applied
requirements.required_evidence: git history of the two files across section closes

requirements.text: DIVISION OF STORES (design decision recorded): the two repo files are the SHARED, loop-visible knowledge stores (D-053-R003: the detached loop and all sessions communicate through the repository - private orchestrator memory is invisible to producers, reviewers, the companion, and the loop, so repo files are the correct medium). Private per-agent memory (.claude/agent-memory/, orchestrator model memory) remains for role-private working notes only; anything program-useful graduates to Tier 1/Tier 2. Format ruling per the owner's 'whichever uses less tokens': terse Markdown pointers (comparable token cost to JSON, better compression via prose ellipsis, renderable everywhere).

RETURN ITEMS - (a) create both files seeded from this session's accumulated knowledge; (b) wire injection: Tier 1 as unconditioned rule, Tier 2 named in the SESSION_HANDOFF must-read list and successor prompt; (c) re-run the session handoff with the new system in place; (d) the owner's verbatim directive is recorded here (the size-budgeted handoff references this capture instead of duplicating the ~800-token reason text).
requirements.required_harness: capture commit contains both files + handoff seq 110 + this registry
requirements.required_evidence: the capture commit; context_budget_check PASS; handoff READY output
